correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the proof for every fixed positive labeled triple. Cylinder clearance implies center distance at least r_i+r_j, which by the cosine law is equivalent to a_ij≥α_ij(λ). The spherical triangle inequality via the antipode of the third point bounds the sum of the three a_ij by 2π. Conversely three gaps in [α_ij,π] summing to 2π give a planar packing with perpendicular parallel axes. Thus the increasing α-sum gives a unique limiting scale. At equality the four external disks are tangent, so Descartes gives the two roots; continuity on the connected positive weight domain and the equal-weight case select the plus root. The optimal angles are strictly in (0,π) and saturate the spherical inequality, forcing the great circle. The three planar center distances are r_i+r_j and form a nondegenerate triangle by strict triangle inequalities. Projection of each other center onto a given axis shows that the direction is perpendicular to both outgoing separations, proving equality rigidity and uniqueness up to the stated symmetries. At deficit ε, total angular slack is O_b(ε); after fixing the first two contact vectors in the canonical plane, the third vector's projection there differs by O_b(ε) and its height is O_b(√ε). Each direction has inner products O_b(√ε) with its two actual outgoing separations by the squared center-distance slack. Replacing those separations by the canonical ones costs O_b(√ε), and the canonical pair is independent, so the in-plane axis component is O_b(√ε). For the twisted axes the cross product of the unnormalized directions is −t(p_j−p_i)+t² det(p_i,p_j)e₃; the scalar triple product hence gives s²/(1+t²H²) for squared line distance. At fixed canonical angles the clearance slack has first derivative −4Λ b_i b_j(2+Λ(b_i+b_j))/[(1+Λ b_i)(1+Λ b_j)] at Λ. Its strictly positive first-order gain as λ decreases allows t=k√ε with a single sufficiently small k>0. Directions differ by tJ(p_i−p_j)+O_b(t²), so all pairs are nonparallel and their separation obstructs any better exponent after any orthogonal transformation. The distinct-weight example gives 23/6.
residual_risks: The 205-case floating-point program was inspected, not run. The estimates are for fixed positive weights and may deteriorate as the labeled weights degenerate.

value.rationale: The result upgrades an extremal value from a ball reduction to a quantitative statement about the actual cylinder configurations. Axis directions are invisible to the elementary center-packing bound. Controlling these directions and matching the rate by feasible genuinely skew triples for arbitrary radii is useful geometric information beyond computing the threshold or perturbing only congruent cylinders.
